notes:
Maintainer risk: MEDIUM — the cryptographic verification path is well-tested with strong independent oracles, but the log-list ingestion seam (PKIX-ppbr.1, PKIX-ppbr.2) has two correctness bugs that undermine the trust-anchor layer for the whole crate, and the public surface (PKIX-ppbr.6, PKIX-ppbr.8, PKIX-ppbr.9) carries pre-1.0 design-closure decisions that need to be made before launch.
Confidence: ~25% chance of missed bug. Least confident flags: PKIX-ppbr.4 (re-encoder bit-exactness across real-world CT-logged certs — only verifiable by running a corpus test). Uncertainty driven by: could not trace SignatureVerifier impl in pkix-path to confirm RSA `parameters: None` and ECDSA DER vs raw signature handling; could not run a real-world precert corpus to validate the x509-cert re-encoder assumption beyond the single committed fixture and live-log capture; could not verify what behavior the Google log_list.json schema specifies for each `state` variant (pending/qualified/usable/readonly/retired/rejected) at the spec level — the bugs in PKIX-ppbr.1 and PKIX-ppbr.2 are filed against the documented intent visible in this crate, not against an external spec read I did. Would raise confidence if: (a) corpus test against ~1000 real CT-logged certs from CRT.sh confirms tbs_without_sct_list round-trips; (b) explicit read of Chrome log_list.json schema documentation confirms state-variant handling; (c) integration test traces SignatureVerifier through to the ECDSA/RSA backend confirming algorithm dispatch.
API contract risk: HIGH — the public surface (SctList, CtLog, SignedCertificateTimestamp, MerkleAuditPath, SignedTreeHead) ships with all-public-fields, no #[non_exhaustive], no serde, no constructor validation, and an Option<u64> log-window type whose two interpretations conflict. Multiple ergonomic frictions (verify_embedded_scts Result<usize>, separate log_id arg on verify_sth, CtLogList missing remove/clear/extend) will force caller-side workarounds within the first 0.x cycle.
API contract confidence: 15% chance of missed issue. Least confident flags: PKIX-ppbr.19 (entry_type contract — the 'add it to the SCT struct' fix may interact with wire-format identity guarantees I did not chase fully); PKIX-ppbr.28 (feature granularity — would need to enumerate every public item to confirm the split into log-list/verify/merkle is clean). Uncertainty driven by: could not run a downstream-consumer integration test to confirm which contract clauses ACTUALLY trip callers (the contract analysis is theoretical without a real second adopter); could not enumerate every potential CtLog field across all CT log-list schemas (Mozilla, Apple, Cloudflare may differ from Chrome's); did not exhaustively check whether pkix-ct's serde feature would interact badly with serde_json/base64 already pulled in by log-list-json (likely fine but unverified).
